# How it works

A run of pi-action checks the request, opens the thread of the issue or pull request, gives pi all requests that have no answer, posts each answer one time, and saves the thread. The main code is in [`src/run.ts`](../src/run.ts).

## The steps of a run

The action is a composite action ([`action.yml`](../action.yml)). Its steps are:

1. **Node.js.** If the Node.js of the job is older than version 24, the action installs Node.js 24.
2. **Dependencies.** The action installs its runtime npm dependencies (`npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts`) in its own directory.
3. **The run** ([`src/index.ts`](../src/index.ts)). See [The run](#the-run).
4. **Save pi thread state** ([`src/push.ts`](../src/push.ts)). This step has `if: always()`. It pushes the thread (and its working-tree snapshots) if the run did not push all of it, for example after a cancellation, a timeout, or a crash.

The action does not change your checkout before the run. In particular, it installs no git hooks: pi follows the conventions of your repository. See [Commit conventions](#commit-conventions).

## The run

1. **Find the request** ([`src/run-context.ts`](../src/run-context.ts)). The request is `pr_number`, or a direct `prompt`, or the event. An event can be a new issue or pull request, a comment, or an answer to a question. pi-action ignores an event without the trigger phrase, and edits of comments other than questions.
2. **Check the author** ([`src/security.ts`](../src/security.ts)). See [Security](security.md#who-can-start-pi). If the author cannot start pi, the run stops and writes a warning to the log.
3. **Acknowledge.** In `comment` mode, pi-action adds 👀 to the comment, issue, or pull request that started the run.
4. **Load models and extensions** ([`src/models.ts`](../src/models.ts), [`src/extensions.ts`](../src/extensions.ts)). See [Models](models.md) and [Extensions](extensions.md).
5. **Open the thread** ([`src/thread.ts`](../src/thread.ts)). pi-action gets `refs/pi/threads/<number>` and `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>` into local refs under `refs/pi-action/` (see [Protection against conflicts](threads.md#protection-against-conflicts)), opens the conversation, and restores the files that the earlier run left uncommitted (see [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity)). If an earlier run did not complete its work, pi continues that work.
6. **Collect the requests** ([`src/triggers.ts`](../src/triggers.ts)). In `comment` mode, pi-action collects all `@pi` comments on the thread that have no answer, not only the comment of the event. The first request of a new thread gets the full context of the issue or pull request. Later requests are follow-ups. See [Prompts](prompts.md).
7. **Work** ([`src/conversation.ts`](../src/conversation.ts)). While pi works, pi-action adds new `@pi` comments to the conversation, and saves the working tree and pushes the thread after each model response and tool result. At `timeout`, pi-action stops pi and reports the timeout.
8. **Report.** For each request, pi-action posts a `🤖 pi Response` comment (or `❌ pi Error`), and adds 🚀 (or 😕) to the request. If pi gives an empty answer, pi-action asks one time for a summary. If a response hits the output token limit (`max_tokens`) without a tool call, pi-action asks pi to continue, up to 3 times in a row and within `timeout`, and then posts an error. In `output` mode, pi-action sets the `response` and `success` outputs and posts nothing.
9. **Save.** pi-action pushes the thread, and writes the git commands that read the thread to the job summary. See [Read a thread](threads.md#read-a-thread).

When a tool from a pi-durable extension asks a question, the run ends after step 7 without a `pi Response` comment. See [Questions on GitHub](extensions.md#questions-on-github).

## The workflow log

The log of the `Run pi-action` step shows what pi does while it works, one line for each step. Click a line with a `▸` to see its details. A run that answers one comment looks like this:

```text
▸ Setup
🤖 nvidia/aws/anthropic/bedrock-claude-opus-5-5 · tools: read, write, edit, bash, typescript · extensions: pit (typescript)
▸ 🧵 Thread refs/pi/threads/46: continuing, started 2026-11-12 07:11 UTC
▶ Request from @cv (https://github.com/o/r/issues/46#issuecomment-1): Ready to write a PR?
💬 I'll look at the existing sessions first.
🔧 bash: git log --oneline -5
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.1s · 5 lines
🔧 edit: src/run.ts (2 edits)
▸   ↳ ✓ 0.0s · 1 line
▸ 💬 I opened PR #48, which ...
✅ Replied: https://github.com/o/r/issues/46#issuecomment-2 (24 model responses · 23 tool calls · 6m40s · 2.1M tokens in, 31k out)
🧵 refs/pi/threads/46 is at 4325d9a
```

| Line | What it shows | Details (`▸`) |
|------|---------------|---------------|
=====

## What pi-action removes from text

[`sanitizeInput()`](../src/security.ts) removes HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) and invisible characters (zero-width space, zero-width non-joiner, zero-width joiner, byte order mark, soft hyphen). People can use them to hide instructions.

pi-action applies it to:

- The text that contains the trigger phrase: the comment, or the body of an issue or pull request that started pi. This gives the task and `{{trigger_comment}}`.
- The title and the body of the issue or pull request (in the built-in prompt, and in `{{title}}` and `{{body}}`), also for `pr_number` runs.
- `/answer` replies, and the titles of questions.

pi-action does **not** apply it to the diff or to review comments. The model gets this text as it is on GitHub. Also, removing hidden text does not stop prompt injection in visible text.

## Extensions

An extension that you load with `extensions` runs inside pi-action, with the permissions and the environment of the job. It can read `github_token`, `api_key`, and all secrets in the `env` of the step. It can change your repository.

- Load only extensions that you trust.
- Pin npm versions (`name@1.2.3`) or git refs (`github:owner/repo#v1.2.3`).
- Prefer a copy that you reviewed and committed to the repository (a path).
- Keep `trust_project` off, unless you trust all people who can change the repository. See [Extensions](extensions.md#trust_project).

## Prompt templates from the repository

A [prompt template](prompts.md#prompt-templates) becomes the request of the user. Anyone who can push a branch can change the files in `.pi/prompts`. Thus, pi-action loads them only with `trust_project: true`. Without it, pi-action writes `Not loading the prompt templates in .pi/prompts: trust_project is off` to the log. Templates from `extensions` and from `agent_dir` load in all cases.

## Thread contents are visible

pi-action stores the full conversation in `refs/pi/threads/<number>`, also the output of tools. It stores the files that pi leaves uncommitted in `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>`, also untracked files that git does not ignore. All people who can read the repository can read these refs. The workflow log shows the arguments of each tool call and the last 30 lines of its output (see [The workflow log](how-it-works.md#the-workflow-log)); GitHub masks registered secrets in the log, but not in the refs. pi-action stops the runner from running workflow commands (such as `::error::` or `::add-mask::`) in the text of pi and in the output of tools. Keep secrets away from the agent, as for all CI jobs. Make git ignore files with secrets, or list them in `worktree_snapshot_exclude`. See [Durable threads](threads.md#read-a-thread) and [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity).

- Tools, commands, event handlers, UI, flags, and all other features of the pi coding agent. The agent keeps the read, write, edit, and bash tools of pi-action.
- `oauth` logins, because they cannot run on a runner. Use an API key.
- Image models and classifier models.

To select a provider from an extension, see [Models](models.md#providers-from-pi-extensions).

## pi-durable extensions

A [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) extension adds its tools and prompt sections to every conversation: comment mode, `pr_number` runs, and direct prompts. An example is the `pit/durable` extension of [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit):

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    extensions: |
      github:cv/pit#v0.35.0   # pit's typescript tool (pit/durable)
```

### Package format

- A package is a pi-durable extension package when its `package.json` has `pi.durable`, a module path. Example: `"pi": { "durable": "./src/durable/index.ts" }`.
- The module exports `createPiDurableExtension(options)`, or a default export with the same signature.
- The function returns a pi-durable `Extension`: `{ name, tools?, sections?, hooks?, wraps?, tasks? }`.
- If a package has `pi.durable` and `pi.extensions`, pi-action loads only the `pi.durable` entry, because its pi extensions need the pi coding agent. pi-action writes this to the log.
- pi-action installs the extensions after its coding tools (read, write, edit, bash). Each extension must have a unique name. Tool names can repeat (see [Override tools and sections](#override-tools-and-sections)).

### Override tools and sections

An extension can change the tools and prompt sections of pi-action and of other extensions:

- **Replace a tool.** A tool with the name of an earlier tool replaces it, as `pi.registerTool` does in pi. For example, an extension with its own `bash` tool replaces the `bash` of pi-action. pi-action writes `pi-durable extension <name> replaces tool bash from coding-tools` to the log.
- **Wrap a tool or a section.** `wrapTool(tool, wrapper)` and `wrapSection(key, wrapper)` of pi-durable change a tool or a section, for example its description or its text. `wrapTool("read", (t) => ({ ...t, callers: ["tools"] }))` hides `read` from the model, but other tools can still call it (see [Tools the model sees](#tools-the-model-sees)).

The order is: the coding tools of pi-action (`coding-tools`) first, then the extensions in the order of the `extensions` input. pi-durable applies the wraps of all extensions in this order. Thus, the last wrap wins.

### Host options

`createPiDurableExtension` receives `{ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log }`:

| Option | Value |
